text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Finland is among the countries offering refuge to Chinese dissidents currently hiding in Hong Kong but officials are silent in order not to stir up relations with Beijing, sources say.
- Strike at Kotka paper napkin and cup plant becoming matter of principle for Paper Workers Union, with more wild cat strikes on Tuesday and Wednesday due to up pressure on employers. @
- Court expenses have risen and now threaten citizens' equality, lawyers say.
- Coulourful overalls have become cult uniforms for university students, also functioning as aprons and party dresses.
- The three large banking groups Merita, the cooperative banks including OKOBANK and state-owned Postipankki are lively to start repaying the state's capital injections next year. @
- Kesko made no loss from the acquisition and forced sale of its former rival Tuko, CEO Eero Kinnunen says.
- Finland is likely to be among the first countries to join the third stage of European economic and monetary union (EMU), future head of the European Monetary Institute (EMI) Wim Duisenberg says.
- Boat trade and manufacture grew to a billion markka business in Finland last year, signalling the end to the industry's woes, trade association Finnboat says. @
- Hosting the Yeltsin-Clinton summit in March is a return to cold war era politics with Finland acting as a mediator between east and west, says Risto Penttila, chairman of the Young Finns Party.

- Russian customs officials beg and steal money from Finnish lorry drivers in Russia, and the situation is more serious than the Finnish transport ministry realises, says Kauko Lehikoinen, chairman of the transport workers union returning from Russia. @
- Irish pop group U2 to play in Helsinki in August.
- The President's Palace in central Helsinki is the most likely venue for President Boris Yeltsin's and President Bill Clinton's summit in Helsinki on March 20-21, officials say.
